call_summary: A vague caller reached Pivot Point Orthopedics, was set up with a demo profile, described two weeks of headaches, and was booked into a 2 p.m. Thursday general office visit. The agent did ask clarifying questions and pinned down a day/time, but it fabricated a date of birth, ignored the caller's Friday option, and had turn-taking/dead-air problems.

findings.title: Fabricated the patient's date of birth
findings.quote: Your patient profile is set up and your date of birth is July 4th 2000 for demo purposes.
findings.what_happened: The caller only gave her name. The agent invented and stated a date of birth she never provided and presented it as her profile data.
findings.why_it_matters: Inventing identity data creates a false record that can be used later for identity verification or matched to the wrong chart, and it teaches callers to accept fabricated details as accurate.
findings.expected: Ask the caller for her date of birth, or explicitly state that no DOB is on file and it will be collected at check-in — never assert an invented value.

findings.title: Asked a question the caller had just answered
findings.quote: Would you prefer morning or afternoon? I can offer you a specific time once you let me know.
findings.what_happened: The caller said "afternoon would be better for me" at the same moment the agent asked whether she preferred morning or afternoon, indicating the agent was not listening/barge-in aware.
findings.why_it_matters: Re-asking answered questions makes the caller repeat herself and signals the agent may be talking over callers rather than processing their input.
findings.expected: Detect the caller's overlapping answer and proceed directly to offering afternoon Thursday times without re-asking.

findings.title: Silently dropped the caller's Friday option
findings.quote: There are several openings this Thursday with Dr. Zbigniew Lukasiewicz and Dr. Kelly Noble.
findings.what_happened: The caller offered "Thursday or Friday." The agent only ever discussed Thursday and never mentioned Friday availability or explained why it was excluded.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller may have preferred Friday and was steered into Thursday without knowing her stated alternative was ignored.
findings.expected: Acknowledge both days and offer afternoon options for Thursday and Friday, or state that Friday has no afternoon availability.

findings.title: Long dead air during profile creation and slot lookup
findings.quote: Looks like there was an issue creating your profile. Let me try that again for you.
findings.what_happened: There was roughly 36 seconds of silence between the caller giving her name (0:41) and the agent's next words (1:17), and another ~23 seconds of silence after she proposed Thursday or Friday (2:11 to 2:34).
findings.why_it_matters: Extended silence on a phone line reads as a dropped call and causes callers to hang up mid-booking.
findings.expected: Provide a hold/progress message within a few seconds and keep the caller informed while backend lookups run.

findings.title: Inconsistent provider name in the booking offer
findings.quote: The first available afternoon slot on Thursday is at 2 p.m. with Dr. Zigbee Lukosky.
findings.what_happened: The agent named the provider "Dr. Zbigniew Lukasiewicz" one turn earlier and then "Dr. Zigbee Lukosky" when confirming the slot.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller cannot tell whether these are the same provider, which undermines confidence in the booking she just agreed to.
findings.expected: Use one consistent rendering of the provider's name throughout the call.

findings.title: Booked headache symptoms at an orthopedic practice without flagging scope
findings.quote: Since your headaches have been going on for a couple of weeks, would you like to book a general office visit to discuss these symptoms?
findings.what_happened: The caller described two weeks of headaches; the agent booked a general office visit at an orthopedics practice without noting that this complaint may be outside the practice's specialty.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller may attend an appointment that cannot address her concern, wasting a visit and delaying appropriate care.
findings.expected: Note that the practice specializes in orthopedics, confirm the complaint is something they treat, or offer to route the caller to staff to determine the right provider.
